Armor isn't about avoiding hits. Hits happen, that's the always-hit rule in action. Armor is about surviving them. Every point of Damage Reduction is one more swing you can take before you go down. Choose wisely.

Shields are different. They add a little passive DR, and they give you a reaction that downgrades an incoming hit. Armor says "I can take it." A shield says "You'll have to do better than that."

{{< pagebreak >}}

## How Armor Works

When you take physical damage, subtract your Damage Reduction (DR) from the damage value. The remainder is what you actually lose from your HP. Simple.

**Example:** Kael wears leather armor (DR 2). A goblin's scimitar hits him for Weak damage (2). 2 - 2 = 0, but damage never drops below 1, so Kael takes 1 damage. The blade scrapes off his hardened leather pauldron. He feels the sting. He doesn't feel the steel.

If the goblin lands a Standard hit (4 damage), Kael takes 2 HP. The armor didn't stop it, but it turned a solid hit into a scratch.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Armor Table

| Armor | Cost | Discipline | DR | Stealth | Notes |
|-------|------|-----------|-----|---------|-------|
| **Padded** | 5 gp | None | 1 | | Quilted layers. Cheap, uncomfortable, better than nothing. |
| **Leather** | 10 gp | None | 2 | | Boiled and shaped. The adventuring standard. |
| **Studded Leather** | 25 gp | 1 Armor | 2 | | Leather reinforced with rivets. Light and quiet, the rogue's choice. |
| **Chain Shirt** | 50 gp | 1 Armor | 3 | Bane | Worn under clothing. Flexible, concealable, noisy when you move. |
| **Breastplate** | 100 gp | 2 Armor | 4 | | Solid chest protection. Leaves arms free for spellcasting. |
| **Half Plate** | 150 gp | 2 Armor | 4 | Bane | Plates on vitals, chain everywhere else. The pragmatic heavy option. Reduces speed by 5 ft. |
| **Chain Mail** | 75 gp | 2 Armor | 5 | Bane | Full-body rings. Loud. Heavy. Effective. Reduces speed by 5 ft. |
| **Plate** | 300 gp | 3 Armor | 6 | Bane | The pinnacle of protection. When you absolutely need to be the last one standing. Reduces speed by 5 ft. |

### Armor and Spellcasting

Armor interferes with the precise gestures and somatic control that spellcasting demands. The heavier the armor, the harder it is to channel magic through your body.

| Armor Type | Spellcasting Penalty |
|-----------|---------------------|
| Padded, Leather, Studded Leather | None, full mobility, full casting |
| Chain Shirt | -1 to spell rolls |
| Breastplate | -1 to spell rolls |
| Half Plate, Chain Mail | -2 to spell rolls |
| Plate | -3 to spell rolls |

::: {.callout-note}
## The Arcanist in Armor

Yes, you can put your Arcanist in Plate. It'll cost you, 3 Armor Discipline ranks at Foreign/Opposed cost (3/6/12 or 4/8/16), plus the armor itself. And you'll cast every spell at -3. Is it worth it?

For most casters: no. You're spending DP to make yourself worse at your primary job. But for a specific build, the battle mage who wades into melee, the front-line Shepherd who heals under fire, a Breastplate (no Stealth penalty, only -1 to casting) might save your life more often than it costs you a spell tier.

The game doesn't forbid any combination. It just makes you pay for unusual choices. That's the Discipline philosophy in one sentence.
:::

## Shields

A shield is an active defense. You're not just wearing it, you're using it. When an attack comes in, you can throw the shield in its path.

The number before each shield is a Discipline requirement: you need that many ranks in the Protection Discipline to wield it, unless it came in your class starting kit (kit gear assumes training, see @sec-chapter-equipment). The full rules live in @sec-chapter-disciplines.

**Buckler (10 gp):** 1 Protection, +1 DR. Small, strapped to the forearm. Leaves your hand free for a second weapon or a wand.

**Shield (15 gp):** 1 Protection, +2 DR. The standard. Wood and iron, carried in the off hand.

**Tower Shield (40 gp):** 2 Protection, +3 DR, half cover. A portable wall. You move at -5 ft speed while carrying it. You can plant it as a maneuver to grant three-quarters cover to one ally directly behind you.

### Shield Block (Reaction)

When you are hit by an attack, you may use your reaction to interpose your shield. Reduce the damage tier by one step: **Strong → Standard, Standard → Weak, Weak → 1 damage.** You must be wielding a shield and be aware of the attack. Reactions in general are covered in @sec-chapter-combat.

Shield Block cannot reduce damage below 1. It can be used against melee attacks, ranged attacks, and spell attacks, anything you can see coming.

> **DA Guidance:** Let the player declare Shield Block after hearing the damage tier result, not before. This makes shields feel active and tactical rather than just a passive DR bonus.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Worked Example: Choosing Your Armor

Roric is building a dwarf Protector at Level 1. He has Brawn +2, Fortitude +1, and the Armor Discipline from his class. He wants to be the party's wall. Here's how he weighs his options:

**Option A, Chain Mail (DR 5, 2 Armor Disc):** He has the Discipline requirement. He pays 2 DP for Armor (2), his class favors it at Home cost (1/2/4). Total DR: 5. He's a fortress. Downside: Stealth Bane, and spellcasters in the party can't rely on him for quiet infiltration.

**Option B, Breastplate + Shield (DR 4 + Shield Block):** Breastplate needs 2 Armor Discipline, he has that. Shield adds +2 DR and the Shield Block reaction. Total passive DR: 6. Plus he can react to downgrade one hit per round. This is the tank build. The shield costs extra coin, but coin is replaceable. Heroes aren't.

**Option C, Plate (DR 6, 3 Armor Disc):** At Level 1, he can't afford Armor (3), that's 4 DP even at Home cost. But he plans for it. At Level 3, he'll buy the third rank and commission a suit of plate. For now, he takes Option B.

Roric goes with Option B. The Breastplate + Shield gives him DR 6, a Shield Block reaction, and he can still move at full speed. At Level 3, he'll reassess. But for now, he's exactly where he needs to be: between the monsters and his friends.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Worked Example: Shield Block in Combat

Roric is holding a choke point against two goblins and their orc warchief. He's wearing the gear he chose above: Breastplate (DR 4) plus Shield (+2 DR). Total DR: 6. The goblins aren't getting through easily.

Remember how this works. The DA never rolls for monsters (@sec-chapter-combat). The DA describes the attack and names the Challenge, and Roric's player makes the Defense Roll. Strong defense means the blow lands Weak, Standard means it lands Standard, Weak means it lands Strong. Roric has Parry rank 1 and a shield in hand, so he defends with 3d6 + Brawn + Parry rank - Challenge.

**Goblin 1 attacks:** "The goblin comes in low, scimitar slashing at Roric's shins. Challenge 1." Roric rolls 3d6 + Brawn +2 + Parry +1 - 1 = 3d6 + 2. He rolls 3, 4, 4 = 11 + 2 = 13. **Standard.** The scimitar's Standard damage is 4. Roric's DR 6 soaks it to the minimum: 1 damage. The blade dings off his breastplate with a sad *ping.*

**Goblin 2 attacks:** "The second goblin circles wide, scimitar raised for an overhead cut. Challenge 1." Roric rolls 3d6 + 2. He rolls 1, 2, 3 = 6 + 2 = 8. **Weak.** The blow lands solid: Strong damage, 6. DR 6 soaks it to the minimum again: 1 damage. Roric doesn't flinch. He's at 11 HP now, and he's only been standing here one round.

**Orc warchief attacks:** "The warchief says nothing. He doesn't need to. His greataxe comes around in a two-handed arc. Challenge 3." This is the one that matters. Roric rolls 3d6 + Brawn +2 + Parry +1 - 3 = 3d6. He rolls 2, 2, 1 = 5. **Weak.** The axe lands for Strong damage: 12.

**Roric's player:** "Shield Block."

He spends his reaction. The damage tier drops one step, Strong to Standard, and the incoming damage is now 9. DR 6 soaks 9 down to 3. The greataxe slams into Roric's shield, ringing off the boss like a temple bell. The haft cracks at the binding, but the blade never reaches his breastplate.

Without the block, Roric takes 12 - 6 = 6 damage, nearly half his 13 HP in a single swing. With it, he takes 3. That's the power of a shield: the warchief's best hit just became a bad bruise, and Roric is still standing in the choke point.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Donning & Doffing

Light armor (Padded, Leather, Studded Leather): 1 minute. Medium armor (Chain Shirt, Breastplate, Half Plate, Chain Mail): 5 minutes. Heavy armor (Plate): 10 minutes. Shield: 1 action.

You won't always have time to suit up. If the party is ambushed while camping, the Protector fights in whatever they were sleeping in. Plan accordingly: sleeping in chain mail is exactly as unpleasant as it sounds.

::: {.callout-note}
## Armor Isn't Just Numbers

The best armor in the game won't save you from a bad position. DR reduces damage, it doesn't make you invincible. Five goblins all attacking the same target will eventually wear down even a Plate-armored Protector through sheer volume of Weak hits.

Use cover. Use positioning. Use the fact that you're harder to kill than everyone else to *control where the fight happens.* The Protector's real armor isn't steel, it's standing in the right place at the right time.
:::
